citation.authors: Wolf AMD, Fontham ETH, Church TR et al
citation.journal: CA: A Cancer Journal for Clinicians

cited_by.title: Colonoscopy: when to start and how often

record.population: US average-risk adults, American Cancer Society 2018 guideline
record.design: Guideline from a systematic evidence review and microsimulation modelling, including an evaluation of the age to begin screening by race and sex
record.finding: The ACS recommends that adults aged 45 and older at average risk have regular screening with a stool-based test or a visual exam, as a qualified recommendation at 45 to 49 and a strong one from 50. The modelling that included race and sex still identified strategies starting at 45; the abstract reports no race-specific start age.
